tracks.legalName: Petition to Seal under G.L. c. 276, § 100A

controllingAuthority.summary: On a form furnished by the Commissioner of Probation and signed under the penalties of perjury, the Commissioner shall seal a record once the statutory period has run. Relief is mandatory and ministerial: no judge is involved, the Commissioner has no discretion to refuse, and no reasons are given. The 2018 Criminal Justice Reform Act cut the waits from five and ten years to three and seven.

exclusions: Convictions under G.L. c. 140, §§ 121 to 131H (firearms), except as part of a delinquency record.
Convictions under G.L. c. 268 or c. 268A, except resisting arrest, which may be sealed.
A person who has at any time been classified as a level 2 or level 3 sex offender under G.L. c. 6, § 178K may not seal sex offences at all.

A guilty finding in Massachusetts within the applicable lookback, or a conviction or imprisonment in another state, a United States possession or a federal court in that window, excepting motor vehicle offences punishable by a fine of not more than $50.

waitingPeriods.condition: Misdemeanour, from the court appearance and disposition including any incarceration or custody

waitingPeriods.duration: 15 years, or for as long as the person is under a duty to register in Massachusetts or any other state where they reside or would be if residing here, whichever is longer

waitingPeriods.condition: Violation of G.L. c. 209A § 7 or c. 258E § 9
waitingPeriods.duration: Treated as a felony, so 7 years

waitingPeriods.condition: Offence that cannot be ascertained to have been a felony when committed
waitingPeriods.duration: Treated as a misdemeanour, so 3 years

geography.venue: Not applicable. One filing to the Office of the Commissioner of Probation covers the statewide record. No court and no caption.

destination.name: Office of the Commissioner of Probation
destination.detail: A single agency filing covering the whole Massachusetts record. Relief is mandatory and ministerial once the criteria are met.

tracks.legalName: Automatic Sealing of Not Guilty, No Bill and No Probable Cause under G.L. c. 276, § 100C ¶1
tracks.publicName: Records that seal on their own

controllingAuthority.summary: The Commissioner shall seal records of a not guilty finding, a no bill returned by the grand jury, or a finding of no probable cause. Sealing is mandatory and immediate; J.F. confirms it. Operational implementation covers records entered on or after March 11, 2024. The only document in the workflow is Form OCPS004, a Request Not to Seal, which exists solely to decline the relief.

exclusions: The defendant's own written request not to seal.
A dismissal is not one of the three dispositions and routes to the judicial sealing track instead.

tracks.legalName: Petition to Seal Criminal Records for Nolle Prosequi or Dismissal under G.L. c. 276, § 100C ¶2
tracks.publicName: Asking a judge to seal a dismissed case

controllingAuthority.summary: A nolle prosequi entered by the prosecutor, or a dismissal entered by the court, may be sealed on petition where the court finds that substantial justice would best be served, which Pon construes as good cause against six factors. There is no waiting period; passage of time is instead one of the Pon factors. Form TC0057 is standardised across the Boston Municipal, District, Juvenile and Superior Court departments.

exclusions: None by offence. This route is not offence-limited, which makes it the fallback for records the administrative sealing route excludes.
An open case is not sealable; for a CWOF the probationary term must be complete and the case actually dismissed.

waitingPeriods.duration: None. Passage of time is a Pon factor rather than a threshold, so a recent case is harder but not ineligible.

geography.venue: Statewide form, court-specific filing. District Court cases are filed at the clerk's office where the case started. Boston Municipal Court cases are filed in the BMC division where the person lives, or, if they no longer live in BMC territory, the BMC division where the most recent eligible record is from. That residence-based venue rule is unique in the state.

destination.name: Clerk's office of the court identified by the venue rule
destination.detail: Boston Municipal, District, Juvenile or Superior Court, per the form's department checkboxes. Prosecutor and victim notice follow; the petition is posted on a public bulletin board pending hearing.

tracks.legalName: Petition to Expunge under G.L. c. 276, §§ 100F, 100G and 100H
tracks.publicName: Expunging a record from before you turned 21

controllingAuthority.summary: Time-based expungement requires all offences to have occurred before the person's 21st birthday, a record of not more than two convictions or two non-conviction records, and three years for a misdemeanour-only record or seven where any felony is involved. The architecture is genuinely staged: the Commissioner of Probation certifies eligibility under §§ 100I and 100J, and only then does the matter reach a judge with the district attorney on notice.

exclusions: The § 100J list: offences resulting in death or serious bodily injury; offences committed with intent to cause death or serious bodily injury; offences involving a dangerous weapon; offences against an elderly or disabled person; sex offences, child sex offences and sexually violent offences; operating under the influence under c. 90 § 24; firearms offences under c. 140 §§ 121 to 131Q; violations of abuse prevention and harassment prevention orders; and domestic assault and battery under c. 265 § 13M.
Any offence occurring on or after the person's 21st birthday. All offences must have occurred before it.
More than two records. Multiple offences arising from the same incident count as one.

Any other Massachusetts criminal or juvenile appearance or disposition, and any out-of-state, United States possession or federal appearance or disposition, excepting minor motor vehicle offences and the records being expunged.
Being the subject of an active criminal investigation.

waitingPeriods.condition: A record consisting only of misdemeanours, measured to include any incarceration, custody or probation

The review identifies no separate participant-facing filing at this stage, so the output is instruction on the objection window, the hearing and what to expect, not a second packet.

tracks.legalName: Petition for Expungement under G.L. c. 276, § 100K
tracks.publicName: Expunging a record created by mistake, fraud, or identity theft

controllingAuthority.summary: Section 100K reaches a record created by false identification or identity theft, an offence that is no longer a crime, demonstrable errors by law enforcement, by civilian or expert witnesses, or by court employees, or demonstrable fraud on the court. It operates notwithstanding §§ 100I and 100J, so the under-21 rule, the two-record cap and the § 100J exclusion list do not apply. The court must find on clear and convincing evidence that the record was created on one of the grounds, then exercises discretion on the best interests of justice.

exclusions: None. Section 100K operates notwithstanding §§ 100I and 100J, so the under-21 rule, the two-record cap and the § 100J exclusion list do not apply. This is the most important structural fact about the track and the internal reference does not state it.

waitingPeriods.condition: A record created on one of the eight statutory grounds

tracks.legalName: Petition for Expungement of Marijuana Offences under G.L. c. 276, § 100K¼

controllingAuthority.summary: Added by St. 2022, c. 180, § 23, effective November 9, 2022. Reaches possession or cultivation of an amount decriminalised by c. 387 of the Acts of 2008, c. 334 of the Acts of 2016 or c. 55 of the Acts of 2017, and possession with intent to distribute or distribution based on such an amount. It operates notwithstanding §§ 100I and 100J. Relief is mandatory: the court shall order expungement within 30 days of the petition being filed.

exclusions: None from within the section. It operates notwithstanding §§ 100I and 100J, so the under-21 rule, the two-record cap, the clean-record conditions and the entire § 100J exclusion list do not apply.
Non-marijuana charges in the same case are not reachable here.

tracks.legalName: Consolidated Multi-Record Sealing Petition in the Boston Municipal Court Department
tracks.publicName: Sealing several dismissed cases at once in Boston

citations: Boston Municipal Court Department Amended Standing Order No. 1-09
controllingAuthority.summary: The Boston Municipal Court Department permits a single consolidated petition to seal three or more criminal records from two or more BMC divisions, under a Standing Order revised after Pon to conform to the new legal standard. It is a local implementation of the ordinary § 100C judicial-sealing remedy, not a separate statewide remedy. Below the threshold, the ordinary route applies with one form per case.

exclusions: Records outside the Boston Municipal Court Department. This does not reach District Court, Juvenile Court or Superior Court records.
Fewer than three criminal records, or records from fewer than two BMC divisions. Below that threshold the ordinary judicial sealing route applies with one form per case.

Records that ended in a finding of no probable cause or a not-guilty finding are outside this consolidated procedure: the May 10, 2024 amended Standing Order 1-09 limits it to dismissal and nolle prosequi records under the second paragraph of G.L. c. 276, § 100C. Those other dispositions arise under a different paragraph of § 100C and their separate procedural and case-law treatment is not decided here; they are not called ineligible for every form of relief (recorded 2026-09-06 from the owner-relayed research).

waitingPeriods.condition: Dismissal, nolle prosequi, no probable cause or not guilty
waitingPeriods.duration: None, the same as the ordinary judicial sealing route.

geography.venue: Boston Municipal Court Department only, keyed by the Standing Order to the division in whose territorial jurisdiction the person resides, read with the general BMC rule that a person no longer residing in BMC territory files in the division where the most recent eligible record is from.

destination.name: Boston Municipal Court division identified by the Standing Order
destination.detail: A consolidated petition supplements rather than replaces the statewide form. The judge may request additional information or documents about the listed cases from the Clerk-Magistrate or the Probation Department.

components.notes: Consolidated petition to seal multiple criminal records, drafted against the required contents and procedure of BMC Amended Standing Order No. 1-09 and the Pon standard, listing every qualifying BMC record across divisions.

Threshold and venue instruction: three or more records from two or more BMC divisions, filed in the division where the person resides or, if they no longer live in BMC territory, where the most recent eligible record is from. Preliminary hearing, public notice and final hearing follow.

rules.filing: File the consolidated petition in the BMC division identified by the Standing Order's residence-based venue rule (the division covering the petitioner's residence; for a non-resident, the division of the most recent applicable criminal record).
rules.fees: No filing fee: the Massachusetts Court System's guide states that requesting sealing has no fee (MA2). Recorded 2026-09-06 from the owner-relayed research; before that date this rule read 'None identified in the review.'
rules.feeWaiver: Not applicable: no filing fee is charged for a request to seal.
rules.notice: The petitioner sends a copy of the petition to the Suffolk County District Attorney's Office at least 30 days before the final hearing unless that office waives the full notice period, and keeps proof of what was sent and when; the court's own notice to the Commonwealth does not remove that obligation. A preliminary hearing is discretionary and the court may proceed directly to a single final hearing; public notice and the final hearing follow under the Standing Order. Any evidence-of-service fields are product completion fields, not a claim that a separately named statutory certificate is universally required. (Recorded 2026-09-06 from the owner-relayed research; previously 'Preliminary hearing, public notice and final hearing per the Standing Order.')
rules.service: The petitioner's own 30-day notice to the Suffolk County District Attorney's Office before the final hearing, unless waived by that office; proof of what was sent and when is kept. (Previously 'Per the Standing Order.')

researchConsolidationScope.statement: The May 10, 2024 amended Standing Order 1-09 limits this consolidation procedure to at least three dismissal or nolle-prosequi criminal records from at least two BMC divisions under § 100C's second paragraph; the Judiciary guide recommends rather than universally requires criminal records or certified dockets. The guide's stop when any hearing is set is a product boundary and is retained; supporting an ordinary uncontested hearing is a separate decision from correctly explaining the published process.

researchFormIdentity.statement: The Standing Order authorizes one petition and says a form is available, but an exact current dedicated consolidated form was not retrieved by the research. Neither unsupported universal assertion is perpetuated: that no such court form exists, or that a TC0057 must accompany every case. The accepted instrument, and whether any per-case forms are required for the selected court, remain to be confirmed with the issuing court; the existing release blocker on form identity stays.

researchParticipantText.text:
Scope. Use this consolidated route for at least three criminal records ending in dismissal or nolle prosequi across at least two BMC divisions. Other dispositions require their own treatment. Confirm the proper filing division and list each applicable docket.

Fee and notice. There is no filing fee to request sealing. Send a copy of this petition to the Suffolk County District Attorney's Office at least 30 days before the final hearing unless that office waives the full notice period. Keep proof of what you sent and when. Court notice to the Commonwealth does not eliminate your separate obligation. Follow the hearing notice; a separate preliminary hearing is not always held.

legalDesignDecision.rationale: Classified as a local_variant non-relief node under the adopted memorandum: the BMC multi-record procedure implements the ordinary § 100C judicial-sealing track locally and is not a separate statewide remedy, so the underlying relief is not double-counted. Re-reviewed under the packet-only model and classified as a single custom_pleading rather than a composed route: the review's stage 1 is threshold and venue routing rather than a legal unit, and stage 3 is hearings, which are post-generation handoffs. No published BMC form was established, and the Standing Order supplies the required contents and procedure, so a controlled consolidated pleading is generated with a local-form override.
